transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CISO - HelixCare), Priya Sharma (Head of IT - HelixCare), Carlos Ramirez (Compliance Manager - HelixCare)

Summary:
Quick posture review focused on SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence availability, trust center access, control mappings, RBAC/SSO (SCIM), audit log retention and format, and encryption/KMS/BYOK options. Customer requested mapping to HIPAA controls and data residency confirmation for eu region. Redwood agreed to share redacted reports and mapping template, and to schedule a technical follow-up for KMS details.

Topics:
- SOC 2 Type II period and redaction
- ISO 27001 certificate and scope
- Trust center access and downloadable artifacts
- Controls mapping spreadsheet (gap analysis)
- RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning
- Audit logging: retention, export, and monitoring hooks
- Encryption: at-rest AES, KMS/HSM options, BYOK
- Data residency and private deployment options

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Ramirez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can kick off — I'm Sofia, AE on this account, and with me is Ethan, our SE. How's everybody doing?
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Good, thanks. I'm Jordan, CISO at HelixCare, we've got Priya and Carlos on as well.
[00:18] Priya Sharma: Hi all.
[00:20] Ethan Chen: Hi team, Ethan here. I'll mostly handle the technical bits. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO artifacts, trust center access, controls mapping, then dive into encryption/KMS and logging. Anything to add, Jordan?
[00:35] Jordan Lee: That sounds right. Our primary asks today: confirm we can get redacted SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO cert, controls mapping to HIPAA and ISO controls, and clarify RBAC/SSO and BYOK options.
[00:48] Sofia Ramirez: Yep. High level, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs in the trust center, we can share redacted reports. We'll also provide a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks — SOC2, ISO, HIPAA — that Ethan will walk through.
[01:05] Carlos Ramirez: Great. On the redaction piece, we can't accept unredacted PII in reports, so we'll need a redacted copy that shows the control effectiveness and exception notes.
[01:16] Ethan Chen: Totally understood. The typical deliverable is a redacted PDF for SOC2 Type II and the ISO 27001 certificate. For the controls mapping we provide a spreadsheet that shows control IDs, description, evidence locations (trust center links), and how they map to HIPAA/ISO.
[01:30] Priya Sharma: And the trust center — is it self-serve access or do we need an NDA?
[01:36] Sofia Ramirez: Trust center access is generally link-based with protected downloads. For certain artifacts we require a signed NDA or a customer portal agreement. We'll include the trust center link in the follow-up email and note which docs need an NDA.
[01:47] Jordan Lee: Perfect. A couple of technical questions — audit logs: retention policy, format, and export options. We need to ingest logs into our SIEM.
[01:56] Ethan Chen: Right. Our standard audit log retention for the hosted offering is 90 days for detailed request logs and 365 for summary events, but for Dedicated or Private deployments we can configure retention. Logs are available in JSON and syslog-compatible formats, and we support push to customer SIEM via secure delivery (TLS). There's also an S3 export option for longer retention.
[02:20] Carlos Ramirez: 90 days is short for our compliance team; can we extend to 2 years for certain event types?
[02:26] Ethan Chen: For hosted API it's constrained for operational cost reasons, but Dedicated / Private allows extended retention and custom hooks. We can capture keystones of events and summarize for longer retention, and full raw logs can be routed to S3 in the customer's account for arbitrary retention.
[02:42] Priya Sharma: So for EU data residency — we have European patients — we need logs and data to remain in eu-west-1. Does Redwood support region locking?
[02:51] Sofia Ramirez: Yes, Redwood supports region pinning on both Hosted and Dedicated; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployments. We can confirm which artifacts in the trust center are region-bound; many compliance docs are global but actual data storage is region-specific when configured.
[03:08] Jordan Lee: Good. Encryption at rest question: do you use a cloud KMS, HSM, and do you support BYOK?
[03:15] Ethan Chen: We encrypt at rest with AES-256. For hosted customers we use managed KMS keys with strong controls; we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via cloud KMS and BYOK for Dedicated/Private. HSM-backed keys are available for enterprise plans. There's a small difference in key lifecycle controls between hosted and private, which we'll document.
[03:36] Jordan Lee: Do you provide key rotation logs and attestations? We need to show KMS usage and rotation events.
[03:42] Ethan Chen: Yes, KMS operations are logged and appear in the audit logs we mentioned. Rotation events are included; we can surface rotation metadata via the trust center or the controls mapping.
[03:55] Carlos Ramirez: About RBAC and SSO — we need SCIM provisioning and granular roles. What role model does Redwood use?
[04:03] Ethan Chen: We support SAML 2.0 SSO with optional SCIM for provisioning. Role model has several built-in roles: Admin, Developer, Auditor, ReadOnly, and a custom role layer that allows us to map narrow permissions (route-level, model-level, billing). For Dedicated/Private customers we can add custom claims mapping.
[04:23] Jordan Lee: Auditing for privileged actions — do you log admin activity separate from API request logs?
[04:29] Ethan Chen: Yes, admin activities are logged in the admin audit trail; those logs include actor, IP, timestamp, action and can be exported separately. They are part of the control evidence for SOC2.
[04:40] Priya Sharma: We're going to need evidence for vulnerability management and pen tests. Do you do annual pen tests and how are results shared?
[04:46] Sofia Ramirez: We contract third-party pen tests annually and have a vulnerability management program. The pentest summary (redacted) and remediation attestations are in the trust center; detailed reports require an NDA. We'll include the pen test summary in the package.
[05:00] Jordan Lee: Can you confirm the SOC 2 Type II period — like start and end dates?
[05:05] Sofia Ramirez: Current SOC 2 Type II reporting period covers 2025-09-01 to 2026-02-28, Type II. We'll include the period in the redacted report.
[05:14] Carlos Ramirez: For ISO 27001 is the scope only platform, or does it include managed services?
[05:20] Ethan Chen: ISO scope currently covers the Redwood platform and control plane across our hosted regions; for Dedicated/Private we have a scoping note and guidance on what the cert covers versus customer-managed infrastructure. We'll attach scope details.
[05:35] Priya Sharma: On controls mapping — does Redwood provide a ready mapping to HIPAA rule sections (164.312, etc.) or is it a high-level mapping?
[05:44] Ethan Chen: We provide a detailed mapping that aligns SOC2/ISO controls to HIPAA sections where applicable; it's a crosswalk spreadsheet. It includes control descriptions, evidence references, and notes where customer responsibility (shared responsibility) applies.
[05:58] Jordan Lee: Shared responsibility — can you call out examples? For instance, encryption of PII at application layer is our responsibility?
[06:05] Ethan Chen: Exactly. We take responsibility for platform-level encryption and network security controls. Application-layer encryption, tokenization, and PII handling in your app are customer responsibilities. The mapping sheet will have a "Responsibility" column indicating Redwood vs Customer responsibilities.
[06:22] Sofia Ramirez: Note — sometimes transcription shows "responsibility" as "responshibility" in our old notes, so just flagging the mapping sheet will be clear.
[06:30] (small laugh)
[06:33] Carlos Ramirez: About logging formats — you said JSON and syslog. Which fields are included? We need user id, request id, model id, timestamps, and geo.
[06:41] Ethan Chen: Logs include timestamp (ISO), request_id, user_id (if provided by customer-auth header), model_id, route, latency_ms, node_id, region, and event_type. For privacy we don't log full prompt text by default unless the customer opts in; prompts can be redacted or routed to customer S3 for retention.
[07:02] Priya Sharma: That's important — we can't have PHI in logs within Redwood for compliance reasons unless encrypted and retained under our controls.
[07:08] Ethan Chen: Understood. For PHI scenarios we recommend routing raw request/response payloads into your S3 bucket (encrypted with your CMK) and keeping only metadata in Redwood logs. We'll document the pattern.
[07:23] Jordan Lee: What about sub-processor lists and vendor management evidence?
[07:28] Sofia Ramirez: We publish a sub-processor list and provide attestations in the trust center. For Dedicated/Private we provide additional details. We'll include the sub-processor CSV.
[07:38] Carlos Ramirez: Any SLAs tied to security incidents? We need notification windows and root-cause remediation timelines.
[07:45] Sofia Ramirez: Incident response SLA: initial notification within 4 hours for high-severity incidents, with a follow-up timeline for remediation and postmortem. These details are in our SOC2 evidence pack and the security whitepaper.
[07:58] Jordan Lee: Can you support entitlements for data exports and deletion requests? We have data subject requests under GDPR.
[08:05] Ethan Chen: Yes, we support export and deletion flows. For hosted customers we have a documented process; for Dedicated/Private we can automate via API calls in your environment. We'll add the deletion proof steps in the mapping doc.
[08:18] Priya Sharma: A network question — do you support private peering or VPC endpoints?
[08:23] Ethan Chen: Yes, Private deployment supports VPC peering and PrivateLink-like endpoints; Dedicated has customer VPC options as well. We'll attach the network architecture doc for review.
[08:34] Jordan Lee: On the topic of evidence artifacts, can we get timestamps on when a control was last tested or updated?
[08:40] Sofia Ramirez: The mapping spreadsheet includes a "Last Evidence Date" column for each control and links to the specific artifact in the trust center.
[08:49] Carlos Ramirez: Who signs attestations? We need a signature from an authorized Redwood executive for procurement.
[08:55] Sofia Ramirez: Yes, executive-signed attestations are available upon request — we'll route it through the legal team and include it with the SOC2 packet where required.
[09:05] Jordan Lee: Great. A quick note on pen tests: can we get CVSS summaries and confirmation that critical findings are remediated?
[09:12] Ethan Chen: Pen test summaries include CVSS scores for findings and an attestation of remediation status. Full reports require NDA.
[09:20] Priya Sharma: If we move to Dedicated, what are the onboarding timelines for security review?
[09:26] Sofia Ramirez: Typical Dedicated onboarding for security and network setup is 6-8 weeks, depending on firewall rules, peering, and compliance review. Private on-prem timelines are longer.
[09:34] Jordan Lee: Okay, good to know. For the follow-up KMS/BYOK deep dive who will lead that?
[09:39] Ethan Chen: I'll lead the technical deep dive and can demo key rotation, CMK setup, and logs.
[09:45] Carlos Ramirez: We'll want details on HSM-backed keys and evidence of separation of duties.
[09:50] Ethan Chen: We'll include separation of duties notes and HSM attestation in the KMS deep dive.
[09:57] Sofia Ramirez: I'll summarize next steps at the end. Anything else on compliance right now?
[10:02] Jordan Lee: One last question on backups — where are backups stored and encrypted?
[10:07] Ethan Chen: Backups are encrypted with the same KMS controls and stored in region-matched S3 buckets; for Dedicated we can push snapshots to your account.
[10:18] Priya Sharma: Can you provide an example retention policy entry for backups and logs? Our compliance team likes to see an explicit table.
[10:25] Sofia Ramirez: We'll add sample retention policy rows in the mapping spreadsheet.
[10:30] (brief pause)
[10:33] Jordan Lee: Great — sounds like a plan. Can we walk through a quick control example to make sure we line up on responsibility?
[10:40] Ethan Chen: Sure. Take logical access control — Redwood is responsible for platform authentication, least privilege enforcement within the console, and logging of admin actions. HelixCare is responsible for provisioning via SCIM, managing SSO assertions, and application-level access to PII. We'll put that as a row in the mapping with evidence links.
[11:02] Carlos Ramirez: That clears it up.
[11:05] Priya Sharma: On the trust center link — can you share a placeholder now so we can see the UI?
[11:10] Sofia Ramirez: I can't paste the live link in the call notes, but I'll include it in the follow-up email and mark which items require an NDA.
[11:18] Jordan Lee: For the redaction type — do you redact account IDs or full email addresses?
[11:23] Ethan Chen: Typically we redact PII like full email addresses and phone numbers and replace with hashed identifiers. Account IDs that are not PII may stay but can be redacted on request.
[11:33] Priya Sharma: Ok.
[11:36] Sofia Ramirez: Quick timeline recap: I'll send the redacted SOC2 and ISO cert by 2026-03-30; Ethan will send the mapping spreadsheet and pen test summary by 2026-04-01; Jordan will provide HIPAA evidence list by 2026-04-03. Then we'll schedule the KMS deep dive the week of 2026-04-05.
[11:54] Jordan Lee: That timeline works.
[11:57] Carlos Ramirez: One small ask — can we get sample admin audit logs to validate fields? Even small sample sanitized logs would help our SIEM mapping.
[12:06] Ethan Chen: Yes, we can provide sanitized sample logs. I'll include a sample JSON export in the mapping package.
[12:14] Priya Sharma: Anything on contractual terms — we might need the security addendum and data processing agreement.
[12:20] Sofia Ramirez: We'll share the standard security addendum and DPA; if you need changes we can route to legal.
[12:28] Jordan Lee: Great.
[12:30] Sofia Ramirez: Ok, unless there's anything else, I'll do a quick recap and next steps.
[12:34] (background noise)
[12:36] Sofia Ramirez: Recap: Redwood will share redacted SOC2 and ISO artifacts, trust center link (with NDA flags), controls mapping spreadsheet, pen test summary, sample sanitized logs, network architecture for Dedicated/Private, and the security addendum/DPA. Follow-ups: KMS/BYOK deep dive w/Ethan, plus HelixCare to send HIPAA evidence list.
[12:57] Jordan Lee: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[13:00] Priya Sharma: Thanks.
[13:02] Carlos Ramirez: Thanks all.
[13:05] Ethan Chen: Thanks, talk soon.
[13:08] Sofia Ramirez: Bye.

Note: timestamps above are approximate; transcription includes occasional mis-hearings and minor typos typical of automated transcription (e.g., "Redwood Dedicated" heard as "Redwood ded nine"). Refer to attached artifacts for authoritative content.
